newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says to agree soon on Indian venture.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says to agree soon on Indian venture.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Thursday it would soon sign an agreement with the Kirloskar group of India to set up a joint venture in that country.
"We will sign an agreement and announce it in the near future," a Toyota spokesman told Reuters. He offered no further details.

Japan's Jiji Press reported on Thursday from New Delhi that Toyota and the Kirloskar group will sign an agreement on Monday at Toyota's headquarters in Toyota, Aichi prefecture, to build a vehicle plant in India.
Jiji quoted Vikram Kirloskar, vice chairman of Mysore Kirloskar Ltd, as saying Toyota would hold 74 percent of the joint venture and the Kirloskar group the rest.
The plant will be built in the southern city of Bidadi, near Bangalore, with start-up scheduled for the latter half of 1999, it said.
The plant will produce 2000cc multi-purpose vehicles, with an initial output rate of 50,000 units per year, Jiji said.

Akira Yokoi, a Toyota executive vice president in charge of overseas business, told Reuters earlier in July that the company was close to reaching an agreement with its Indian partner and that a pact was likely by August 9.
